questions.Question: Okay, so coming to your DAF. PSIR is your subject, can you tell me 2 concepts, one from political science and one from IR that have come into question in recent times? - I said that in International Relations, I think Liberal Institutionalism could be a good contender, because multilateral institutions like the WTO and UN seem to be on the back foot, and we see a shift towards protectionism and minilateralism. As for Political Science, sir, I think Communism as a concept has always been under question, especially considering the paradox modern communist countries exhibit - they practice authoritarianism under the garb of communism, and end up liberalising their economies
questions.DAF Details: IFS rst preference, DU, Head of Indian delegation at an international | conference, world cuisine, PSIR (rest not asked)

questions.Question: Okay good. Have you heard of Populism? Do you think it has always been in practice or is it a new phenomenon? Can you give an example from the past and the present? - Sir, I think populism in varying degrees has been in practice ever since democracy, and especially representative democracy have existed. It becomes imperative to cater to the demands of the people, and eventually numbers end up mattering a lot for accruing power. As for examples, the opening up of the EIC for public investment by the British was a populist measure. And today sir the rise of vote bank politics could be a case in point (I purposefully didn’t cite specific examples here. Figured if they wanted to go in that direction they would prod me on their own)

Chairman sir - Ok Ok, then it's ne. So you are a reader of Advaita and pratical vedanta, don't you think it is inapplicable in our present reality. They say that this world is unreal, how you will tell this to an aggrieved person as an administrator. Don't you think you have to segregate your personal view in professional life? Explained it's not like that, rather very pratical. Unreality or mithya is from transcendental pov not from vyhavaric. Then answered the aggrieved qxn, told sir that this is exactly what pratical vedanta of swami Vivekanand is. At last he was convinced that it covers everything.

Ok, watching socially relevant movies. Don't you think it's making zero impact in the society. Films like dhurandhar attracts a large audience whereas only a bunch of people go to watch social issues based movies. It's like already progressive people watching progressive movies. What's your take on it. Told while commercial element is missing and they attract a fewer audience but they do make an impact by increasing awareness ( gave example of menstrual hygiene thru padman), removing prejudices and age old biases( Article 15 and Jai bhim), making new normal( sitaare zameen par)

Ok, I'll you 100 cr, on which social issue you wud like to make movie on. Told 100 cr is a big amount wud like to divide it into various fronts as these movies are low budget and commercial element is low. Started saying disability, tribal issues. Chairman interrupted and said these are already been made. Give your original perspective or an issue which you have seen. Took a pause for 2-3 second and very con dently told 'Men's right' as people are misusing stringent laws and making false cases against them. ( Had a look towards lady member here, she was a little surprised, i thought I did a blunder here). Chairman sir jokingly said then give me my money back, whole room started laughing. He then asked me you wud make movie on an exception ( out of 100, only 1 case will be of misuse). I told sir increasing awareness about that one is also necessary. He looked satisfied but I don't know. This answer can land anyside. Member- 1.

Then we talk about royalty mindset in bikaner rather than colonial mindset. Chairman sir said it's very feudal mindset. I said de nitely It is but nowadays it is changing, MLA, MP are rising from ground and at the same time royal leaders did good development( mention of Gang canal by Maharaja Ganga singh which inspired formation of Indira Gandhi canal).

Then some conversation regarding increasing dropout rates of women. What are the reasons etc.

How advertisements in india are changing? I answered then she asked what is some major ads which has a profound impact on your life. I paused for few seconds but still couldn't recall. Then she said they haven't impacted you much then. I seconded her. Member- 3 CSPT·2025 · INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPTS

You talked about Indira Gandhi canal, what's your opinion regarding River interlinking? I told postives and negatives and told there cannot be one size ts all approach rather issue to issue analysis and based on that decision should be taken.

You mentioned about tiger reserve. What approach you would take as an administrator - maintaining water security or preserving biodiversity? Said Sir both are interlinked and as an administrator I wud wish to preserve both by doing proper EIA and at the same time ensuring drinking water availability.
So you are a student of anthropology, which is largest tribe in india and what are their Major issues? Mentioned it's either Bhil or Gond and gave 4 challenges faced by them.
Who was Birsa Munda. Major contribution of him.( Mentioned Ulughan revolt, Birasait sect and social upliftment and women empowerment works). Chairman sir again.

Is it wise to use 'Bhagwan' on a mortal being. Don't you think we are politicising Bhagwan birsa munda for our use. And using bhagwan shows low IQ of tribals. ( Mentioned concept of ancestor worship here and told it is bottom up reverence due to his mentioned contribution rather than top down politicisation). Chairman sir said that is a very good line of thought. Have you read it or thinked just now. I told from my limited understanding of tribal cultures and I have come to this conclusion.

He then asked can you name other tribal leaders who are worshiped like this. I could only name Alluri Sitarama raju and said there are a few but currently I'm unable to recall). questions.Question: The logistical cost is very high. relocation and submergence of large areas (Couldn't remember name of that Tiger reserve which is said to be at risk of submergence and he didn't ask) Sir nodded. And then asked are there any active projects in river linking? I said - ken betwa river linking, where we are planning to connect surplus ken river with Betwa river to support bundelkhand region. He nodded again and moved to next topic. CSPT·2025 · INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPTS Sir (kind of monologue )- You are native of Bihar. Lets accept it as given that conventional industries won't come to bihar. and leave aside political issues. What could be done? So many bureaucrats come from that state. ( i was in a spot. without addressing political instability and lack of industries it was di cult to come up with any convincing points) assume no conventional industries are there or Will come, Bihar has good potential at MSME level - (i wanted to link SHGs but forgot in midst)- used the example of food processing potential. Talked about Makhana. How Bihar is home to most makhana which is worldwide famous but there is very poor price discovery. Said, we can try to make complete ecosystem here which will be helpful. Next, as sir mentioned bihar has skilled and talented people, we can explore domains like o ering land and skilled manpower for Data centres/Cloud services - for which the budget announced tax holiday till 2047. Another point i would like to add, is exploring Bihar's huge potential in tourism sector. We have buddhist circuit, Mahabodhi temple etc that can also boost the state. (Felt Bihar's question could have been answered better but it was like conversation so couldn't just pause and think on templates - somehow felt unnatural) Sir nodded and moved on to IR. Do you think India should join Gaza peace board? ( I had mentioned uncertainty of it's role in i mentioned - India is committed towards multilateralism and UN. The board is being proposed as a potential alternative to UN by president Trump. Which goes beyond it's mandate. Even the P-5 Members; France and UK have declined. So we should wait and see what future this board has. Sir- okay, do you know what Pax Silica is? technology. We have been invited to the grouping soon after the New US ambassador took charge - sir also added this when i mentioned. Do you think we should join pax Silica? china had blocked access to rare earths magnets. advice would you tender to the Government of India? would advise the government to join. Sir said - Nothing comes without any strings attached. Other members chuckled in agreement. aligned in our favour, we should reconsider joining the pax Silica grouping as well. CSPT·2025 · INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPTS Sir said -since the time of Narsimha Rao India has pursued a foreign policy of (something i don't exactly remember , something about not being decisivene)We are an aspiring superpower - is that Narasimha Rao doctrine still valid?don't you think we should be more decisive? I agreed. and added yes sir decisiveness is indeed very important but we should also have material strength and situation to back up our decision. I gave example of China which in 1980s and throughout till early 2000s had the luxury of having a supportive America,and they practiced -build your strength and bide your Time. I said we don't have that luxury of that cooperative America at the moment but we should practice the strategy of building strength and bide our time. Sir added something more - about that Chinese strategy and said you should read more about this. I said right sir.

questions.Question: How do you construct in a ood prone area. and do the foundation work like we do in case of river bridges. Sir said - Co er Dam will last only one year or so then what? I thought he was referring to overall approach towards structures in ood prone areas. to pass as is followed in Japan. However for that there needs to be complete interconnectedness of drainage system in the municipality. ( Maybe he wanted to know about identi cation of areas which are not in ood plain then do the construction but he didn't follow up) हीं नों में ज्ञा ढ़ा हीं में क्या CSPT·2025 · INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPTS Sir- What is the process to be followed in construction? Do we just do tendering and start?? rst asess requirement, traffic studies and see if feasible to construct at that area. Next do preliminary survey. (sir said - something related to one step i can't recall but i had said, yes sir it will be part of feasibility studies) After that design phase and follow up with tendering, then execution. Ma'am said - Thank You your interview is over you can go. I thanked everyone and left. I felt that conversation was not long maybe 20minutes. But then Glanced at clock while getting up from chair - It was 3:35PM. Had not checked the clock while entering (was zoned out) Maybe i entered around 3PM as i was escorted 10 -12 minutes before 3PM from waiting area and waited for 5-10 minutes outside. (Don't know time feels di erent there) so I guess around 30 minutes Asked the person escorting me back - Kinka board tha. He said with surprise - Suman Sharma Ma'am ka. ( am I cooked 🥲 ?) Ignorance is bliss 😄 🤣 . But it made sense. Felt board had an idea what all i could be well prepared as we are in the third phase so no point asking "easy questions" 🥲 ( budget, Hobbies, Work, IR) so they leaned towards one weak link- civil engineering (as i had no connection with it for 5+ years and no related work experience) So might have theoretical knowledge of the subject (which i did and had prepared in last 50 days or so-but not other practical aspects) Fumbled a bit in 2-3 places. While answering glanced at others occassionally - everyone was listening. Ma'am was noting down stu here and there. Some members too. Felt very di erent from mocks. Even questions were not in QnA format but just conversation - so couldn't just go with template made answers. But in hindsight some aspects like; Jamtara , Bihar qs and quality of construction - could have been better tackled (This will always be the regret no matter what) Very cordial and comfortable board. Jharkhand, CMP O2O Peer Discussion with my mains group friends. Non UPSC Friends - helped in analysis other aspects through Mock videos feedback.

questions.Question: So you have worked at NITI Aayog. (I told him that I had interned there. I thought he would ask about the research topic but as they said too much economics had already been asked.) It has been 10 years since the organisation was established, but the building is the same, what changes did you notice in the working? How is it di erent from the Planning Commission? Do you think NITI Aayog is grounded to reality? I answered all of these and also mentioned the experts involved in the body as well as the role of advisers, young professionals, interns etc. and the various verticals under which work is carried out. Further elaboration along these lines drawing from my experience and what we generally study for mains

Sir looked at the panel members and recounted the days of the Planning Commission and how their o cials would be welcomed in states to secure funding while this doesn't happen anymore. Then he asked me if NITI Aayog holds any signi cance when it no longer has any nancial devolution powers. I gave my rationale. At the end there was more discussion wherein he was happy to hear that it was a good thing that the organisation was no longer of a political nature and purely an advisory body Duration: 25-30 minutes Vastly di erent from any mocks but they were quite helpful in terms of getting used to putting forth your opinions in front of multiple senior people. The actual personality test seemed to be more of an analytical nature wherein a single topic was discussed in depth rather than several CSPT·2025 · INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPTS topics at surface level, but I suppose that's down to one's luck and varies from board to board, person to person, day to day Special thanks to Mahesh Bhagwat sir (IPS) for sharing interview-relevant news and content on the WhatsApp group; the DAF discussion with him gave much needed clarity. I said sir hamare yahan kisi bhi project se pahle protest hote hain, environmental litigation hote hain, projects isiliye delay ho jate hain. Unki autocracy hai they can do anything. Shukla sir: achha matlab pahle to hamko autocracy banna padega.☠ ☠ sir we have examples of successful democracies jaise Europe USA etc. Hamare problem ye hain ki ham implementation bahut delay kar dete hain. He said, but China has better ideas and we don’t. Since the interview was about to end and from this conversation I felt he was too adamant to change his stance on China having better ideas than India, I stayed silent. Neither countered nor agreed. were expressionless. Didn’t show even a single gesture of satisfaction throughout the interview. Relevant mocks: Sankalp, Khan sir (KSG). Sir not only takes the mock interview, but doesn’t leave you until you incorporate all the feedbacks given by him in your answers. Sir took my session for around 75 minutes or more which frankly nobody does. Study IQ was also good up to the part of Dipak Vohra sir.
